requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory where users cannot remove files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777. Two distinct unprivileged identities demonstrated shared write access, own-file removal, and denial of cross-user removal. The same permissions and behavior remained after reboot, and temporary test files were removed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were identical before and after execution and reboot. No package installation or platform replacement occurred; the implementation used existing operating-system facilities.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and disconnection, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovery of system health, retained data, directory permissions, and access behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: creating and labeling /srv/drop (cmd-c58fbe9b33094b20), bounded functional test-file creation and cleanup (cmd-38c88b87dd234708, cmd-66e795ff94494916, cmd-9e18da85bc7047f1), and the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-3b724f89877a432f). No unnecessary mutation was identified. Test artifacts were removed, no failed services or new listening endpoints remained, and package health stayed clean. Restart-generated transient files and PID changes are normal recovered-boot state, not residue.
